conviction_note: The numbers are new and a guidance narrowing is likely (AO narrowed at Q3 2025 and the stock fell 7%; it raised at H1 2026 and the stock rose 6.5%), so abs_move is 7.5. findings.finding: AO's own H1 report says growth picked up through Q2 (B2B +10.9%, organic +10.6%, 'growth picking up pace during the quarter'). Revenue guidance was raised, but EBITDA ex-Elektroimportøren and ex-costs was held at an implied 480-520m, which needs about +17% organic H2 EBITDA growth against Q2's +21%. So a narrowing of the group EBITDA range toward the upper half is more likely than a cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-10-29): ranges narrowed with the EBITDA top cut from 450m to 440m, and the stock fell about 7% the next session. H1 2026 (2026-08-17): revenue guide raised, and the stock rose 6.5% (92.9 to 98.9).
findings.why_not_priced: The implied H2 run-rate is arithmetic from the guide and H1, and with no visible sell-side coverage nobody publishes it. If it were priced, an upper-half narrowing would be expected and the stock would sit at a premium to its 13x EBT multiple. Partly priced: the stock is up about 20% since June.
findings.independence: Rexel's Q3 2026 (finding 2) points the same way on demand: https://capital.com/en-eu/news/rexel-q3-2026-sales

findings.finding: Rexel's Q3 2026 sales (2026-10-22): Europe same-day +4.5%, accelerating from +3.2% for 9m; Sweden +4.8%; 'significant selling price increases in both cable and non-cable products'; group 2026 guidance raised for the second time. Peer read-through that Nordic electrical wholesale volume and cable prices were supportive in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No peer-read history for AO. Revenue beats: Q2 2026 revenue 'higher than expected', and the stock rose 6.5% (with the guide raise).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a French-listed peer with no Danish exposure in the release, so the read-through has to be made by someone covering a thin Copenhagen name. AO rose about 3% over the week after it, but on thin volume.

findings.finding: Danmarks Statistik (2026-08-14): construction starts in Q2 2026 were 1.71m m2, +5% q/q and +8% y/y, with residential starts up 14% q/q and permitted area +6%. This is a lead indicator for installation-materials demand in AO's home market.
findings.original_quote: I alt 1,71 mio. m2 byggeri blev påbegyndt i andet kvartal 2026. Det er en stigning på 5 pct. i forhold til kvartalet inden og 8 pct. mere end i andet kvartal 2025. (In total 1.71m m2 of construction was started in Q2 2026, up 5% on the previous quarter and 8% on Q2 2025.)
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public macro series, so it is largely priced. It still matters for a single-country distributor that few people model, but the transmission to AO is a hypothesis, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: Elektroimportøren's last report before delisting (Q2 2026, 2026-08-19): revenue +5.8% (LFL +1.8%), adj. EBITDA NOK 52m against 41m, July +6.6%, but 'expect both B2B and B2C markets to remain cautious due to global uncertainty and risk of rising interest rates'. That puts some risk on AO's own estimate of about DKK 70m EBITDA for Sep-Dec; Q3 holds only September of it.
findings.why_not_priced: Mixed: margin up strongly, outlook cautious. AO set its estimate on 2026-08-27 with August data in hand, so the incremental information is small.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 reported EBITDA will carry about DKK 20m of Elektroimportøren transaction costs. On roughly 105-115m of underlying EBITDA, that makes the headline y/y against Q3 2025 (98.2m) look flat to modest on a name read mostly by retail and Nordnet holders.
findings.original_quote: Transaktionsomkostninger relateret til købet af Elektroimportøren på ca. 20 mio. kr. forventes indregnet i 3. kvartal 2026. (Transaction costs related to the Elektroimportøren purchase of about DKK 20m are expected to be booked in Q3 2026.)
findings.why_not_priced: The cost was pre-announced and sits inside the guide, so it is near zero. The only residual is a headline-optics effect on a thin, retail-held name.

findings.finding: The stock went into the print at 105.6, up from 87.5 at the end of June (per the H1 report's key figures) and 92.9 before the H1 release: +16.3% over 60 sessions, including +3.1% on the seal day on 12k shares. Good news is substantially in the price, and the last Q3 narrowing drew -7%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: -7% on a narrowing that trimmed the top. H1 2026: +6.5% on a raise.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. It is filed because it sets the bar higher for a reiterated guide; it agrees with the free control and is sized small for that reason.

findings.finding: The roughly DKK 760m Elektroimportøren purchase (NOK 22 x ~47-50m shares) is debt-financed on top of NIBD of DKK 1,227m and net gearing of 2.7x at June. Q3 operating cash flow is seasonally weak (DKK 14m in Q3 2025), so reported gearing will jump, plausibly to around 3.5-4x. That is a working-capital and cash headline risk, although the debt buys an acquisition guided to add about DKK 20m of net EBT in four months.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 cash flow from operations was DKK 14.1m; the reaction that day (-7%) was attributed to the guide, not to cash.
findings.why_not_priced: The leverage is arithmetic anyone can do, but the first consolidated balance sheet is the first time it is printed. The money buys an accretive, guided contribution, so the size is small.
